limits: The load harness runs the single-process local Node runtime with file-backed JSON state, not Cloudflare Workers, Durable Objects or SQLite-backed object storage
Client and server share one 12-logical-CPU, 16 GB Windows machine, so CPU, disk and event-loop contention are not representative of Cloudflare placement
The local runtime caps a room at 20 members and a host at 10 active rooms; the test sizes rooms to the member cap
The workload measures steady-state socket liveness, 2-second polls and one host action per room, not full bidding, chat, history paging or reconnect storms
The 500 and 1,000-user failures include HTTP fetch failures and pong timeouts; the exact root cause was not isolated
The intended 10-second steady-state window stretched to 40.1 s at 500 users and 32.2 s at 1,000 (31.1 s in the probe); this is a symptom of event-loop and request contention, not a longer test
The 100-user pass is a measured local result for this workload, not a capacity guarantee; no 500-user or 1,000-user capacity and no Cloudflare capacity is claimed
wrangler and Miniflare were unavailable offline, so the Workers runtime, bindings, SQLite-backed object storage, hibernation, alarm delivery and 101 upgrade were not executed
Browser and accessibility runs exercise the unchanged local Node runtime, not the Worker or Durable Objects
No deployment, account setting, cloud resource, R2 activation, credit card charge or production migration was created
